content.title: About
content.content: Candy Fruit Flavored Pieces are small fruit‑flavored bites coated with a sweet shell. Made from sugar, fruit flavorings and colorants, they deliver a bright berry and tropical fruit taste with a pleasant chewy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The range includes more than 10 flavors such as strawberry, orange, grape and mango.
Each batch undergoes quality control to ensure consistent sweetness and color intensity.
Fruit flavorings are derived from natural extracts, complemented by artificial enhancers for a stronger taste.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, reducing the product’s environmental footprint.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The sugar in the candy is rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Vitamin C in certain flavors
items.content: The “Citrus Mix” flavor is fortified with vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive sugar can contribute to tooth decay and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain trace amounts of nuts, soy and dairy, which are important for people with allergies.

items.title: Not suitable for children under 3
items.content: Small pieces can pose a choking hazard for toddlers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candy as a standalone snack, mix into dessert blends, use in baking, or as a decorative topping for cakes. It is recommended not to exceed the daily recommended sugar intake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. For extended shelf life, keep refrigerated to prevent melting and texture changes.

content.title: About
content.content: Candy “Fruit Snacks” are small soft treats made from fruit puree, sugar, and gelling agents. They have a bright fruit flavor, a pleasant chewy texture, and are often coated with a light sugar glaze. The product is marketed as a sweet alternative to traditional candies, suitable for both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial launch of fruit snacks took place in the United States in the 1980s.
The formulation often includes natural fruit purees, but flavorings and colorants may also be used.
They are typically sold in single‑serve packets of 30–50 g.
In some countries they are classified as “confectionery” rather than “fruit” due to high sugar content.
Fruit snacks are frequently packed in school lunch boxes as a quick source of energy.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Some varieties are fortified with vitamin C, which supports the immune system and provides antioxidant protection.

items.title: Source of quick carbs
items.content: Sugar delivers a rapid energy boost, useful during physical activity.

items.title: Small amount of fruit
items.content: The inclusion of fruit puree adds a modest portion of fruit to the diet.

items.title: Mood enhancer
items.content: Sweet taste stimulates serotonin production, helping improve mood.

items.title: Convenient to eat
items.content: No preparation needed; they can be eaten straight from the package.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some recipes may contain gluten, soy, or nuts, which is important for people with allergies.

items.title: Not a substitute for fresh fruit
items.content: Although fruit puree is present, they lack the fiber and most vitamins found in fresh fruit.

items.title: Artificial additives
items.content: Many versions use artificial colors and flavors, which can cause sensitivity in some individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candy “Fruit Snacks” are convenient to eat straight from the pack as a snack, add to kids’ lunch boxes, or use as a sweet component in desserts such as yogurt or ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place, sealing the package tightly to prevent drying out and moisture absorption. For longer storage, keep in the refrigerator, but do not freeze.

content.title: About
content.content: Lentil curry is a fragrant Indian dish made from red or green lentils, tomatoes, onion, garlic, ginger, and a classic blend of spices such as turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and chili. The dish is rich in protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates, making it a hearty and nutritious meal for vegetarians and anyone seeking a satisfying entrée.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lentils are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for more than 8,000 years.
Traditional Indian curries are often cooked in clay pots (kadhai), which enhance the aroma.
In Indian cuisine lentils are called "dal," and dal curry is considered a comfort food in many households.
The spice blend in curry provides antioxidant properties and may aid digestion.
The recipe can be easily adjusted for heat level by varying the amount of chili or adding coconut milk.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Lentils provide about 18 g of protein per 100 g of dry weight, making them an excellent protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron from lentils is better absorbed when paired with vitamin C‑rich ingredients like tomatoes or a squeeze of lemon.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Turmeric, cumin, and coriander contain polyphenols that may reduce inflammation.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Lentils raise blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for blood‑sugar management.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lentils or other legumes.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes contain oligosaccharides that can cause flatulence; soaking and proper cooking reduce this effect.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should consume lentils in moderation.

items.title: Salt and fat
items.content: The dish often includes added salt and oil; those with hypertension should monitor quantities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot lentil curry with basmati rice, naan, or flatbreads. Garnish with fresh cilantro, a dollop of yogurt, or a squeeze of lime for brightness. Leftovers store well in the fridge and can be reheated on the stove or in a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked curry in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to a rolling boil before serving to ensure safety.
